sample_unit: patient and carer questionnaire respondents (plus 37 healthcare professionals; 34 matched pairs in workshop)

links.outcome: Change in agreement on trust, acceptance and benefit of AI after structured educational session
links.effect: Agreement rose from 38.2% to 67.6% (trust), 85.3% to 97.1% (acceptance), and 52.9% to 97.1% (perceived benefit) in 34 matched pairs; all p≤0.003.
links.quote: Agreement (‘agree’ or ‘strongly agree’ combined) with statements relating to trust, acceptance and perceived benefit of AI was significantly higher after a structured educational session (38.2% to 67.6%, 85.3% to 97.1%, and 52.9% to 97.1% respectively; all p≤0.003).

unlisted_practices: Using the term 'machine learning' rather than 'artificial intelligence' in patient communication increases trust
Regulatory approval of diagnostic AI as a driver of patient trust
Phased AI-assistant-first deployment with validation and audit checkpoints for pathology AI

screen.practice: structured patient education session before AI deployment
screen.reason: Empirical mixed-methods survey and focus group study measuring patient, carer, and clinician views on AI in histopathology, directly testing the effect of a structured educational session on stakeholder trust and acceptance before and after.
